title: Detention and Recipe
premise: Seventeen-year-old Casper Marchetti has spent a decade being the responsible one—cooking, cleaning, and raising her younger siblings while their mother works hospital night shifts. When the ghost haunting Hollow Creek High begins leaving her handwritten notes in ink that vanishes by morning, Casper realizes the spirit knows her name, her secrets, and the truth about the fire that took the school's old home economics wing twenty years ago. As the notes pull her into an investigation entangled with her grandmother's lost recipe book and a friendship built on a lie she told years ago, Casper must choose between protecting her carefully managed invisibility and telling the truth about who she really is. In the end, revealing what happened the night of the fire frees the ghost, mends her broken friendship, and teaches Casper that belonging means letting herself be seen—even when it costs everything she thought she needed to hide.
about_author: Dominic Oyelaran is a former high school custodian who spent years listening to students' stories after hours and now writes them down instead. He lives near an old boarding school he swears is haunted, where he tests every recipe in his books on his very skeptical nieces.

chapters.title: The Careful Girl
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A morning in the Marchetti household: packing lunches, waking siblings, forging mom's signature on a permission slip. Establishes Casper's exhausting competence and her rule of invisibility at school. Emotional beat: love expressed as labor, and the loneliness inside it.

chapters.title: Detention, Table for One
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Caught with contraband groceries during class, Casper earns Saturday detention in the old west wing—the wing gutted by fire two decades ago. Her best friend Priya covers for her with a lie, deepening Casper's guilt. Emotional beat: resentment flickering under gratitude.

chapters.title: First Note
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Alone in detention, she finds a note tucked under a scorched desk: 'You burn the rice on Tuesdays, Casper Marchetti.' The ink shimmers and fades before her eyes. Emotional beat: terror laced with the shocking thrill of being known.

chapters.title: Ink That Won't Stay
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Casper and her brother Theo, who notices her distraction. Casper photographs the second note; by morning the photo is blank too. She researches the 2005 fire and finds a photo of a home economics teacher who never left the building. Emotional beat: obsession taking root.

chapters.title: Priya Knows Something
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya watches Casper slip away again and recognizes the look from fifth grade, when Casper lied about why she missed Priya's birthday. Priya's own family secret—her mother's deportation case—makes her fierce about honesty. Emotional beat: friendship strained by silence.

chapters.title: Grandma's Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Digging through her late grandmother's things, Casper finds a recipe book with pages torn out—and handwriting identical to the notes. Grandma Marchetti once taught at Hollow Creek High. Emotional beat: grief reopening, inheritance becoming literal.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Terms
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The ghost—Miss Odalys Ferrer—communicates through chalk dust and fading ink: she will tell Casper about the fire only if Casper brings her the missing recipe pages. First direct contact. Emotional beat: bargaining with something that sees straight through you.

chapters.title: Little Lies at Home
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo covers for Casper's absences with the littlest sibling, mimicking the caretaking he learned from her—but he's scared of how far she'll go. He finds the recipe book hidden under her mattress. Emotional beat: the cost of secrecy rippling through the family.

chapters.title: Page One: Salt
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Following a clue in grandma's annotations, Casper retrieves a page hidden in the library's card catalog. Miss Ferrer's story begins to surface: she was blamed for the fire. Emotional beat: dawning doubt about the official history.

chapters.title: Caught in the West Wing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya follows Casper into the burned wing and catches her talking to empty air. Confrontation: Priya demands the truth; Casper lies badly. Priya walks out. Emotional beat: the friendship cracking exactly along the old fault line.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Mom's shift is cut and she's home at dawn, exhausted, and finds the house in disarray from Casper's midnight searching. A raw argument about who carries this family. Emotional beat: Casper saying the unsayable—I'm tired of being careful.

chapters.title: Page Two: Fire
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The second page reveals the fire started in the chemistry lab, not the kitchen—and that a student set it, a student whose family buried the blame. Casper recognizes the surname: it's on the school's biggest donor plaque. Emotional beat: righteous anger meeting fear of consequences.

chapters.title: The Donor's Daughter
chapters.summary: New POV: Marisol Vance, daughter of the donor, a popular senior who has been leaving anonymous flowers in the west wing. She knows what her aunt did as a girl and has been paying penance in secret. Emotional beat: guilt inherited like money.

chapters.title: Allies in Detention
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper and Marisol collide in detention and trade truths. Marisol confirms the cover-up; Casper shares the pages. They plan to restore Miss Ferrer's name publicly. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance, the first team Casper has ever had.

chapters.title: Theo Runs Away (Two Blocks)
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Overwhelmed and feeling replaced by Casper's new mission, Theo takes the little one and hides out at the corner store until midnight. Casper finds them; the siblings have it out honestly for the first time. Emotional beat: found family sharpened into real family.

chapters.title: Page Three: Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The final page isn't evidence—it's a letter: grandma knew Miss Ferrer was innocent and stayed silent to protect her job. Casper must decide whether exposing the truth also exposes her grandmother. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden, not just gift.

chapters.title: What Casper Told Priya
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper goes to Priya's house and tells everything—including the fifth-grade lie, which wasn't laziness but shame about her family's poverty. Priya doesn't forgive instantly, but stays. Emotional beat: truth offered without guarantee, and received anyway.

chapters.title: The Centennial Assembly
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At the school's centennial assembly, Casper, Priya, Marisol, and Theo stage their reveal: the restored recipe pages projected behind the principal's speech, the true account of the fire read aloud. The room erupts. Emotional beat: terror turning to triumph mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Smoke and Light
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the west wing that evening, Miss Ferrer appears fully for the first time—not vengeful, just tired. She thanks Casper, tastes the dish Casper cooked from the completed recipes, and lets go. The ink stops fading. Emotional beat: release, and the ache of goodbye.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Public and Private
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Fallout: the district investigates, the Vance name is quietly removed from the plaque, and Casper becomes briefly famous—which she hates. But Priya defends her in the hallway, publicly choosing her. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not performed.

chapters.title: Sunday Dinner
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Mom, given day shifts at last, cooks alongside Casper and the kids using Miss Ferrer's finished recipe book—a new Marchetti tradition begun from an old wrong righted. Emotional beat: abundance after scarcity; care shared instead of carried alone.

chapters.title: Notes, Addressed by Name
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, epilogue. Months later, Casper finds one last note in her locker—in ordinary pen, signed by three friends inviting her to start a supper club in the rebuilt kitchen. She writes back in fading-ink replica as a joke, then signs her full name. Emotional beat: invisible no more, and glad of it.
